answer: A new key earns a trial only after an independent hydrographic office validates one randomized chart correction near a public jetty. The agent must cite harbor soundings and tag the correction with a jetty/harbor/atlas nonce; an officer signs its unique chart/edition ID, and the registry consumes that record, rejecting duplicate or unsupported changes. Proposed review fee is .60 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .60 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,600 (1,000 × .60). Limitation: chart data and reviewers are unevenly available and may collude.
